lead.headline: Talks End in Abu Dhabi; News Moves to Moscow and Dublin
lead.deck: Russia and Ukraine agreed to swap prisoners, but not to stop fighting.
body: Two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, a city in the United Arab Emirates, ended on Wednesday. Russia and Ukraine agreed to exchange prisoners of war. These are soldiers captured by the other side.

The teams did not agree to a ceasefire, which is a stop to the fighting. They also still disagree about land. Jared Kushner, an American who helped run the talks, said the final number of prisoners would be set on Thursday.

Now the news moves to two more cities. Kushner and Steve Witkoff fly to Moscow, Russia’s capital, to meet President Vladimir Putin. Then they go to Dublin, in Ireland, to meet Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

world.headline: Scientists Say the World Will Burn a Little Less Fuel This Year
world.deck: More than 140 scientists shared their count at a meeting in Turkey.
body: Burning oil, gas and coal puts a gas called carbon dioxide into the air. It warms our planet. Each year more than 140 scientists add up how much the world makes.

Their new count came out on Tuesday at a climate meeting in Antalya, Turkey. It says carbon dioxide from these fuels will fall 0.4% in 2026, to 38.2 billion tonnes. It falls in China and the United States, but rises 4.4% in India.
Fires and damaged forests add carbon dioxide too. Counting everything, the total rises to 43.3 billion tonnes.
